steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: 'Out of safety considerations, the connector must be... the most suitable replacement material...'

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The expected amount of materials needed... Could it be...?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No, these are early notes. She would have crossed them out if there were a mistake.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: How big could this Eye of Iberia be?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: When lit, its light would be seen from every single window in Gran Faro...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Now that's got to be a myth.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Luminosity testing... Well, the diagrams are very clear. Should only be a matter of following them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But the town doesn't seem to have the materials needed for the prototype...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: One second! Coming!
The young caretaker hastily stuffs the notebook into a drawer, picks up his lamp, and hurries through the chapel.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's very late. What brings you to the—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: —A Messenger?! What the...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Take it easy. You can lean on my shoulder.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Just sit down by the door. I have some clean gauze.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Close the door...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A-Alright.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Clean cut. Took the belt with it.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I should be able to treat it.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But it'll be a few days before you can move again.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: That was close.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yes, sir, it's good that you came quickly. There isn't much I could have done if the wound got infected.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: You're not going to ask how I got hurt?

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Or is everyone in this town like this?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-I just thought stopping the bleeding was more urgent...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't really know how to answer that question, though. I don't know how things are anywhere else.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Very few people come to Gran Faro. And those who leave don't come back.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: I guess that's the kind of place this is... Close to the sea, and close to the Inquisition.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Exactly... even Messengers like you don't stay for long.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Sorry, I forgot to ask your name. Messengers come and go in a hurry; they don't often stop at the chapel.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: I'm... ahem. Do you know Gran Faro well?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I guess? I grew up here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But as for the things that happened here a long time ago... about the plaza, the statue there, and the sea... I only know them through my uncle's stories.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: That's plenty.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Sorry to ask this of you after you've already done so much for me... but there's something I need help with.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: This package is for Gran Faro, but it doesn't say who exactly the recipient is or where they live, only 'the door with a white flower on it.'

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: White flower? That doesn't ring a bell...

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: I'm afraid I'm not in any shape to go on a search around town for a few days.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: But I won't sleep easy until this package makes it to the recipient.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Alright, leave it to me.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Whoa, it's heavy...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll go once the sun rises.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll get you a couple more blankets. They're old, but they'll keep you warm.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: ...Be careful.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Young folks this days are so careless! At this rate, they'll draw the Inquisition here, ruining the peace that we've had for the last twenty years!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Always telling me to calm down and be reasonable... since when has the Inquisition been reasonable?!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The rest of the soup is yours, lad. A bit too salty for my tastes... Anyway, be careful. Don't draw attention to yourself.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Alright, Uncle Thiago. I'll take it easy with the salt next time.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Did something happen in town?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: It's nothing, just people nosing about in Gran Faro again.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Two snooping priests from the Inquisition. Heaven only knows what scent they're after.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But whatever it is, Gran Faro doesn't have it. Can't they tell? There's nothing left here.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...Anything happen at the chapel? Are you still reading your parents' notes?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yeah... they're pretty interesting. The whole day went by before I knew it.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't let anyone see you reading them. They're in Ægirian, aren't they?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know, Uncle Thiago. I'll be careful.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I only left them there because I thought the most dangerous place to hide them would be the last place they'd look. I didn't want those Inquisition thugs taking everything from Gran Faro.

spans.text: I only left them there because I thought the most dangerous place to hide them would be the last place they'd look. I didn't want those Inquisition thugs taking

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I never even considered whether anyone would read them.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But I suppose it's worth it, if it helps you pass the time.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm really grateful that you preserved them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: By the way, there was a visitor at the chapel—

steps.name: Voice Outside the Door
steps.text: Thiago! Are you there? There's something we need to deal with before the Inquisition sets its eyes on our town!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: (Whisper) Jordi!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A-Alright! I'll stay in my room and lock the door...

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Apparently, those priests were chasing a Messenger, not one of us.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: The problem is, they suspect him of carrying messages for the Ægir.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: ...Don't give me that look, Thiago. We've got nothing against the Ægir; it's them, not us.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Anyway, we went to the chapel. The Messenger got hurt in a scuffle with the priests and took refuge there.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...The chapel?

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Don't worry, we waited for Jordi to leave before we brought them there. No one said a word about him.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: We all like the kid. We're not about to drag him into this mess.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Anyway, the Messenger gave up his luggage for the priests to search through. They didn't find anything suspicious, though.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Probably another misunderstanding.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Ha, a misunderstanding!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...Alright, I get what's going on.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Let's keep our heads low for a few days. Don't even bring it up.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Once this blows over, it'll be as though nothing ever happened. The Inquisition won't bother us again.

steps.name: Excitable Townsfolk
steps.text: Alright, I'll let the others know.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A suspicious package sent by an Ægir...
Jordi picks up the package behind the door, wrapped in dark-green cloth, and takes a sniff.
Did the smell of salt come from the bundle in his hands, or from the damp air enveloping Gran Faro throughout the four seasons?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I'll go look myself.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The townsfolk are all good people. I don't think they'd do anything so bad that they should be taken away.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle Thiago told me many Ægir used to live here. Maybe someone sent this to a friend, not knowing they had moved away.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I'll find out who the recipient is!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So, nothing on the east side of the plaza.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll save the rest for tomorrow morning... Uncle said those priests start patrolling at 7 am. I should get home quickly.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Hopefully they'll be leaving soon... It's been three days, after all.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A door with a white flower on it... but most of the houses here are painted white anyway. A white flower wouldn't go well with them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait, did I see something white by the door of that one?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, I guess I was mistaken...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's not a flower, but... a book?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Weird... no one has lived here for a long time, but the book is new.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Let's see... I'll try knocking.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Sounds like there's no one here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Still no answer. Guess I must have been overthinking this.

steps.name: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.text: I'll go up this street. You take the other side. Kick the door in if something doesn't look right.

steps.name: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.text: This is the only part of town that we haven't searched.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (Unfamiliar voice, unfamiliar accent... must be those priests.)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (I have to hide!)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (I might run into them if I head back this way.)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (It would be a headache for Uncle Thiago if they find me...)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (The footsteps are getting closer.)

steps.name: Gentle Female Voice
steps.text: Good morning. Visitors here are few and far between, much less one so accomplished at such a young age.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (The door opened? And I've heard that voice before...)

steps.name: Young Priest
steps.text: My accomplishments pale in comparison to those who've already reached the rank of Inquisitor at my age.

steps.name: Young Priest
steps.text: You seem to share our faith more than most of the residents here, rather than simply blindly fearing the judgment of the Inquisition.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: I've gained a smattering of knowledge from the works I've read. At the very least I know what the Inquisition is up against.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: If what you fear is really in this town, I suggest you look over that way.

steps.name: Young Priest
steps.text: You have a lead?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: No, I've never seen anything out of the ordinary. That's why I chose to live here, in this quiet town, where I can focus on my work.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: However, the sea is that way.

steps.name: Young Priest
steps.text: You mean it could only be outside of town... I see. Of course, that is more than ordinary priests like us can handle.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Good morning, Jordi from the chapel.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Er, good morning.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Just a question... is this package for you?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Why yes, it is. Thank you.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Phew, glad to know.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll be going, then.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Don't you want to know what's inside?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh? Oh, no, of course I'm not suspecting you.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You're more knowledgeable than anyone in Gran Faro. Uncle Thiago said you've given him a lot of good ideas.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It's okay. You can come in. It can't hurt to set your mind at ease, can it?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: I had this abandoned house patched up to hold all the documents I don't have space for at home.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: And... perhaps someone would come here, someday, to read the stories of Gran Faro, Iberia, and beyond.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The package you delivered was more books.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It's in Ægirian. Can you read it?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Er... barely, I guess.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...So it really was sent by an Ægir.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Feel free to peruse it, if you like. Since you can read it.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: This one is about plays... some sort of stage setup...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Designs for a theater... they look amazing.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are you studying drama, Ms. Amaia?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Of course not. I'm but a humble translator.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: A friend of mine found these lying around at home. Some Ægir must have written them from memory after the disaster.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Disaster?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Ah, never mind.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Anyway, she sent them to me, hoping I could translate them into Iberian.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It's hard to preserve the writings of the Ægir in this land-bound country, after all.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, yes, it could cause misunderstandings if they were seen by priests who don't know Ægirian.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...You sounded sad. Is it because of what happened to the Ægir?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Perhaps... but it's more than just them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Well, I've gotten used to this life... I'm fine with it.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know I can't exactly speak for all Ægir, though.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Do others also live like this, in other places?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: What it's like in other places... Well, Jordi, would you like to help me with the translation, seeing how you're the only Ægir here?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It would certainly save me from having to flip through that old dictionary so much.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh? I-I'm not sure I can handle something so difficult...

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: It's okay. You can just help out anytime you feel like it.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You can also look through any books here that catch your eye, of course.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Words may deceive at times, but it's undeniable that they break through barriers and unlock new possibilities.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Including things regarding the world outside that you're so curious about.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Now, where did my teapot go? Have a seat, Jordi. Stay a while, and you may find something that interests you here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry, I have to get back to the chapel. Someone needs to care for that injured Messenger.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Thank you for the offer... but I need to do my job as a nurse first.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: That young man... does he not understand?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Has he not dreamed of having wings, gazing at the boundless ocean from above, at the waves melting back into the water?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Jordi? Where did you go?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You said you would be back before 7. I told you to stay put. Those priests are probably leaving today.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: S-Sorry, Uncle.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I was going to tend to the Messenger, then stay inside.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Those young folks already saw to the Messenger. They want you to stay home without worrying about him.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Alright, I'll thank them next time... I'll stay put here today.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll be right here, okay? I'll close the door and read under the lamp.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: That lamp... it works?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I just followed what it said in the notes. I don't know if it's actually fixed, but it's giving out light now.

a.text: 'I heard about it, Thiago. You folks are erecting a proud new building on land, while we go and rebuild the Eye of Iberia.'
'I saw the foundations. They are deep. Perhaps it will be a reminder of Iberia's Golden Age, when it's finished.'
'Gran Faro will not be so grey and dull when we return. The lighthouse will shine here, and the Inquisition will build this place up.'
'Can I ask you something, Thiago? Try to hang this lamp in that building somewhere.'
'That way, I can be a part of its construction too.'

steps.text: I'm sorry I couldn't hang the lamp here... not in this chapel that the Inquisition uses to spy on Gran Faro.
It's broken, anyway, ever since the night the Penal Battalion garrison charged out from the chapel.
I'll put it in a box with your notes. Maybe they'll be preserved, if they're lucky, but I dare not pray for it.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...Keep reading, lad.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I'll be going.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, Mr. Messenger. You're awake.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Those priests have left Gran Faro. No need to worry now.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: And I delivered the package. Don't worry, I saw what was in it, and it was nothing bad. It's all a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: ...Rald.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: My name is Rald.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Sorry. Being a Messenger tends to bring its share of trouble, and I didn't want any more of it than necessary.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I'm Jordi. And I understand.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Anyway, your wounds are healing well. You should be able to move around normally in a couple of days.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Do you like this place, Jordi?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I don't know. Why do you ask?

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: This place is too close to the Inquisition, and maybe has had too much history with it. It's filled with danger, and forced to remain in this gloomy state.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Especially for an Ægir.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: I don't want to spend one more day here than I have to. Have you never thought about leaving, and seeing what's out there?

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: You could come with me, if you don't know where to go.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: The northern wilds may seem dangerous, but I know a relatively safe way.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: I also know a few cities that are more tolerant of the Ægir.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Ægir like you have a chance to dream, and realize those dreams.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Dreams...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Do people out there know the sea better?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Do they talk about the great lighthouse, about the legend of the Eye of Iberia?

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Don't be silly, Jordi. The people don't really talk about the sea. As for the great lighthouse, that's a nursery tale that the people of Gran Faro tell their children.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Thank you for the offer, Rald.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I can't go, not until I've seen the sea and the lighthouse.

steps.name: Local Messenger
steps.text: Gran Faro has failed. The dream of Iberia's Golden Age ended decades ago.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Don't say that.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's not just a dream for Iberia. It's also a dream for the Ægir...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...For one Ægir.
